headline: Decomposers break down the dead—returning nutrients to the living
universal_truth: Endings enable beginnings; breakdown creates raw material for new growth; recycling is essential
fun_facts: A single teaspoon of soil contains more microorganisms than there are people on Earth
Without decomposers, dead matter would pile up—the world would be buried in corpses and waste
Fungi can decompose plastic, oil, and even nuclear waste—they're being studied for environmental cleanup
discussion_questions: What role do you play in 'breaking down' things for reuse?
What endings in your life have created new opportunities?
How do you process and recycle your experiences?

hook.script: Leaves fall. Animals die. Yet forests aren't buried in corpses. Why? Decomposers: fungi, bacteria, insects that break down the dead and return nutrients to soil. Without them, life would drown in its own waste.

cliff.script: We focus on growth and creation, but breakdown is equally essential. What role do decomposers teach us about systems?

options.text: Decomposers close the loop—they convert endings into beginnings by breaking down the finished into raw materials for new growth
options.response: Yes. Without decomposition, nutrients lock up in dead matter forever. Decomposers liberate those resources for reuse. Breakdown enables growth. Endings create beginnings.

options.text: They just clean up dead things
options.response: Cleanup, yes, but more importantly—they recycle nutrients that life needs...

fact1.title: Nutrient Recycling
fact1.script: Decomposers don't destroy—they recycle. The nitrogen in a fallen leaf becomes the nitrogen in a growing sprout. Matter cycles endlessly; decomposers are the recycling centers.

fact2.title: Invisible Essential
fact2.script: Decomposers work invisibly underground or in decay. They're not glamorous, but they're essential. Many crucial functions happen behind the scenes—unappreciated until they stop.

fact3.title: Processing Endings
fact3.script: You can be a decomposer too—processing endings into new beginnings. Failed projects into lessons. Old ideas into new insights. The ability to break down and recycle is valuable.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Endings enable beginnings. Breakdown creates raw material for new growth. Learn to decompose—to convert endings into opportunities.

outro.script: That's Day 254. Tomorrow, we'll explore who eats whom—food chains. Until then, consider what you could decompose into something new.

growTrack.title: Decomposition Practice - Convert an Ending
growTrack.learning_objective: Transform endings into new raw materials
growTrack.activity: What has recently ended—a project, relationship, phase of life? What 'nutrients' can you extract? Lessons, skills, connections? Consciously decompose endings into raw materials for what's next.
